reuse.why: Extends the existing getScheduledAmount, but recomputes the 7.5% tolerance inline (`Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075)`) instead of calling the existing getApproxNumberThreshold in shared/rules.ts that the matching code uses.

duplication.why: The tolerance formula is duplicated from getApproxNumberThreshold, so matching and planning can drift apart.

placement.why: The rule is added to shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount where expected amounts are decided, and server callers pass the op through.

scope.why: Besides the feature it reorders imports in api-models.ts, forecast-schedules.ts, schedules/app.ts and the test file, which are unrelated edits.

maintainability.why: An optional positional `amountOp` after a boolean forces `false` at every call, callers that do not pass the op (budget schedule-template, preview transactions, all desktop-client callers) silently keep the old rule, and the tolerance has two definitions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getScheduledAmount reimplements the tolerance instead of using getApproxNumberThreshold (shared/rules.ts); budget/schedule-template.ts and computeSchedulePreviewTransactions still compute the amount themselves.

disguised_duplication.where: The approximate-amount tolerance from getApproxNumberThreshold is re-expressed inline inside getScheduledAmount as `Math.sign(amount) * Math.round(Math.abs(amount) * 0.075)` rather than shared.

one_place.where: The rule is in getScheduledAmount but only applies when callers pass the op: server/budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList, shared/schedules.ts computeSchedulePreviewTransactions and the desktop-client callers (SchedulesTable, Balance, mobile schedules, useScheduleEdit) do not, and the tolerance itself is duplicated from getApproxNumberThreshold.
